_doc: Industry-wire headline catalog (slice #176, expanded #177, parent #150). Each template is keyed by a structural TRIGGER (what happened in the engine) and carries its own SOURCE (who is talking) and RELIABILITY tier (how much the player should trust it). Reliability is the load-bearing axis: 'direct' already happened and is verifiable on the lot or at the block; 'leading' is a forward call fired AHEAD of a shock that may be a false alarm; 'lagging' only confirms a trend the player could already see in their own numbers. Slot placeholders are filled at fire time from live state: {segment} (plural segment label), {pct} (absolute magnitude as a whole percent), {label} (shock catalog label), {brand} (rival brand), {days} (lead time in days). Copy lives here, not in code, so wording retunes without a build. #177 added three voices — trade press (a fictional pub, mostly forward calls plus lagging texture), factory bulletins (direct, and only for the shocks the factory actually causes) and competitor watch (direct, the tracked-with-numbers sibling of vague lot talk) — plus `shockSources` and the weekly market report.
_shockSourcesDoc: Which voice announces a given market shock, by shock id from data/market-shocks.json (#177). A recall or an incentive program comes from the factory; a fuel or credit story is trade-press macro; anything unmapped falls back to the whole pool for the trigger, so a new shock never goes unannounced. Selection is filtered to the mapped source; if that source has no template for the trigger the engine falls back to the full pool rather than dropping the headline.

reliabilityNotes.direct: It already happened — you can verify it.
reliabilityNotes.leading: A call about what's next. It may not pan out.
reliabilityNotes.lagging: Catching up to a trend your own numbers already showed.

weeklyReport._doc: Weekly market report copy (#177). The report is the trade pub's longer-form column, published on the configured weekday and standing on the Home screen until the next one replaces it. It is NOT a wire headline — it never spends the daily headline budget and never appears in the ticker. `summaries` are picked by the week's SHAPE: 'up'/'down' when the movers agree, 'mixed' when they pulled against each other, 'quiet' when nothing cleared the reporting bar. `forwardCalls` are the desk's own bets for the coming week and are deliberately fallible — a 'shock' call reads the scheduler's future arrival roll (and is only made some of the time), a 'drift' call just extrapolates the week's momentum. Slots: {segment}, {counterSegment} (plural labels), {pct} (whole percent), {days} (lead time).
